strategy.summary: src/cart.js already implements cartTotal (bulk discount, SAVE5 coupon, shipping). Unit tests with Vitest must prove each AC through the public functions cartTotal/bulkDiscount, including the boundaries (10 items, $50, $0 floor) and refusal of unknown coupons. Reading the code shows bulkDiscount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount, against AC1 and the constant's own doc comment ("at least this many"): that case is expected to fail and will be recorded as a defect.
inScope: cartTotal and bulkDiscount in src/cart.js: bulk discount threshold, coupon handling, $0 floor, shipping threshold, empty cart
outOfScope: Line-total/subtotal behaviour already covered by test/cart.test.js
Any UI or checkout endpoint (none exists in the repo)
assumptions: Coupon codes are case-sensitive: 'save5' counts as 'any other coupon code' and is refused (the code does this).
Refusal with an error means cartTotal throws; the test checks the error names the submitted code rather than matching the whole wording.
Amounts are compared rounded to cents, as cartTotal returns them.
openQuestions: bulkDiscount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`; AC1 and the BULK_THRESHOLD comment say 10 or more. Is the off-by-one a defect (assumed) or is the ticket wrong?

risks.description: Off-by-one at the bulk threshold (exactly 10 items)
risks.mitigation: TC1 tests exactly 10 items; TC2 tests 9.

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount, or shipping threshold computed before discounts
risks.mitigation: TC4 picks amounts where each wrong order gives a different total; TC7 reaches $50 only after the coupon.

risks.description: Negative goods total when the coupon exceeds the goods

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets none.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, with the goods never below $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when the goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

testCases.title: gives 10% off a cart of exactly 10 items
testCases.expected: 31.99 (30 - 3 discount + 4.99 shipping). Expected to fail today: code returns 34.99 (defect, marked it.fails).
testCases.rationale: Boundary of AC1; the code uses > instead of >=.

testCases.title: gives no bulk discount to a cart of 9 items
counts items across lines by quantity for the bulk discount
testCases.rationale: Proves quantities are summed, not lines counted; 11 avoids the boundary defect.

testCases.title: takes SAVE5 off after the bulk discount
testCases.expected: 53.99 (60 - 6 - 5 = 49 goods, below $50 so + 4.99). Coupon-first would give 54.49.
testCases.rationale: Order of discounts and shipping judged after discounts.

testCases.title: ships free when the goods reach exactly $50 after discounts
testCases.rationale: Free-shipping boundary, reached only after the discount.

charges nothing for an empty cart

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items gets 10% off. bulkDiscount in src/cart.js uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so exactly 10 items gets no discount (the BULK_THRESHOLD doc comment itself says "at least this many"). Expected cartTotal([{price:3,quantity:10}]) = 31.99, actual 34.99.
defects.evidence: src/cart.js:22 `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`; TC1 asserting 31.99 fails (marked it.fails, run passes as expected-failure).
